record.original_question: Whenever a pair of spherical space forms of a fixed dimension has the largest possible volume among all isospectral non-isometric pairs in that dimension, must that extremal pair always be a pair of lens spaces?

evidence.quote: Question 4.7. Are isospectral and non-isometric spherical space forms of largest volume always lens spaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A spherical space form is a Riemannian manifold of the form $\Gamma\backslash S^n$, where $S^n$ is the unit round sphere of dimension $n$ and $\Gamma$ is a finite subgroup of $O(n+1)$ acting freely on $S^n$ by isometries, equipped with the quotient metric. Two such space forms are said to be isospectral if the spectra of their Laplace–Beltrami operators (counted with multiplicity) coincide, and isometric if there exists a Riemannian isometry between them. A lens space is a spherical space form of odd dimension $2m-1$ obtained as $L\backslash S^{2m-1}$ for some cyclic subgroup $L$ of $O(2m)$ acting freely.

Fix a dimension $n \geq 2$. Among all unordered pairs $(M_1, M_2)$ of $n$-dimensional spherical space forms which are isospectral but not isometric, suppose that the common volume $\mathrm{vol}(M_1) = \mathrm{vol}(M_2)$ attains the maximum possible value over all such pairs (assuming such a maximum is attained in dimension $n$).

Question: Must every such volume-maximizing pair consist of two lens spaces?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been addressed for odd dimensions: in dimension $2n-1$, the maximum-volume isospectral non-isometric pair is known to consist of lens spaces for all $3 \le n \le 1000$ except possibly $n = 144$ and $n = 935$, with general partial results bounding volumes (e.g., pairs of volume $\ge \mathrm{vol}(S^{2n-1})/10$ are isometric). The general question across all dimensions remains open.

status_evidence.title: Isospectral spherical space forms and orbifolds of highest volume
status_evidence.snippet: Confirms that highest-volume isospectral non-isometric pairs of spherical space forms in dimension 2n-1 are lens spaces for 3 ≤ n ≤ 1000 except n=144, 935.
status_evidence.claim: Partial confirmation in odd dimensions up to 2·1000-1 with two exceptions.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2305.10950v2
status_evidence.snippet: Question 4.7: Are isospectral and non-isometric spherical space forms of largest volume always lens spaces?
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open problem.
